item.text: The research pass has now covered each selected chapter at least once, with contrary searches interleaved rather than front-loading Chapter 1B or 7B. The strongest recoveries are Chapter 1B’s 2022 disarmament/nonproliferation record, Chapter 2B’s parliamentary arms-delivery debate and export data, Chapter 3B’s independent police-complaint record, Chapter 5B’s distributional/relief implementation evidence, Chapter 6B’s service-access study, and Chapter 7B’s prosecutor-linked document-search record. I’m consolidating these as provisional units and preserving unresolved attribution.

Continuation research completed across all eight selected chapters. No scores were assigned.

The workspace remained read-only and the shell failed to initialize, so `research-ledger-manifest.json` could not be updated directly. The following append-ready units continue numbering from R052.

### New evidence units

- **R053 — 1B:** Germany’s 2022 disarmament report records participation in the NPT Review Conference, TPNW observer meeting, Stockholm Initiative, and NPDI. It also records German–IAEA efforts to secure Ukrainian nuclear plants. Target-period policy evidence; formal government attribution, but not personally Scholz-directed. Contrary limitation: the report does not establish nuclear restraint rhetoric or operational command decisions. Supports `1B.2`, `1B.4`, `1B.5`, `1B.6`, `1B.8`. [Federal Foreign Office report](https://www.auswaertiges-amt.de/en/aussenpolitik/themen/disarmament-report-2022-2594380#content_1)

- **R054 — 1B:** The same 2022 report documents German biosecurity work, cyber-policy initiatives, controls on lethal autonomous weapons, and a pledge not to conduct destructive anti-satellite tests. These are distinct catastrophic-risk governance actions, mostly Foreign Office-led and institutionally attributed rather than personal Scholz conduct. Supports `1B.7`, `1B.9`, `1B.10`. [Federal Foreign Office report](https://www.auswaertiges-amt.de/en/aussenpolitik/themen/disarmament-report-2022-2594380#content_1)

- **R055 — 2B/8B:** In the April 2022 Bundestag debate, opposition leader Friedrich Merz accused Scholz of delaying and avoiding decisions on heavy weapons; other speakers warned both of escalation and of insufficient diplomacy. This is contemporaneous contrary political evidence, not an independent finding of improper conduct or policy failure. Supports `2B.1`, `2B.3`, `2B.6`, `2B.8`, `2B.9`, `8B.5`, `8B.8`. [Bundestag debate](https://www.bundestag.de/dokumente/textarchiv/2022/kw17-de-selbstverteidigung-ukraine-891272#604470)

- **R056 — 2B:** The Bundestag recorded the weapons already delivered by April 27, 2022, including anti-tank and air-defence systems, ammunition, and the planned Gepard ring exchange. This independently documents implementation chronology, while the minister’s legal characterization and effectiveness claims remain official. Supports `2B.3`, `2B.4`, `2B.5`, `2B.8`, `8B.2`, `8B.5`. [Bundestag government questioning](https://www.bundestag.de/dokumente/textarchiv/2022/kw17-de-regierungsbefragung-889556#604371)

- **R057 — 2B/8B:** The 2022 arms-export report states that Ukraine received 26.9% of German export-approval value and that 92% of approvals went to EU, NATO, or NATO-equivalent states. It also cautions that aggregate approval values are not a sufficient measure of restrictiveness. This provides formal scale and an important methodological limitation, not proof of civilian effects or end-use compliance. Supports `2B.3`, `2B.4`, `2B.5`, `2B.8`, `2B.9`, `8B.2`, `8B.3`. [Bundestag summary of the 2022 export report](https://www.bundestag.de/presse/hib/kurzmeldungen-995934)

- **R058 — 3B:** Saxony’s independent police complaints body received 261 complaints in 2022; 28 were substantiated and 74 partly substantiated, while 19 complaints triggered criminal investigations and two triggered disciplinary investigations. This is target-year incident-level evidence of a functioning complaint channel and substantiated police concerns, but it is subnational and cannot be attributed to Scholz personally. Supports `3B.1`, `3B.4`, `3B.7`, `3B.8`. [Saxony police complaints report](https://www.polizei.sachsen.de/de/96990.htm)

- **R059 — 3B/4B:** A Bundestag government response recorded continuing threats and violence against journalists, including 22 new cases by February 2022 and a substantial pandemic-protest connection. This establishes adverse press-safety conditions and public reporting, not executive direction or tolerance by Scholz. Supports `3B.5`, `3B.8`, `4B.6`, `4B.7`, `4B.9`. [Bundestag response on threats against journalists](https://www.bundestag.de/presse/hib/kurzmeldungen-901644)

- **R060 — 4B/3B:** A December 2022 Bundestag record states that the federal government regarded disinformation as a potential threat to public security, social cohesion, and radicalization control. This documents an official governance concern and response frame, but not the effectiveness of countermeasures or any suppression of opposition speech. Supports `4B.3`, `4B.6`, `4B.7`, `4B.9`, `8B.4`. [Bundestag response on disinformation](https://www.bundestag.de/presse/hib/kurzmeldungen-927772)

- **R061 — 5B/6B:** The Bundestag recorded that the third relief package had a 2022 volume of €13.3 billion, including a €6.3 billion pensioner energy payment and a €3 billion energy-cost programme for firms. This provides implementation and fiscal-scale evidence; it does not establish adequacy or distributional success. Supports `5B.3`, `5B.8`, `5B.9`, `6B.1`, `6B.3`, `8B.2`, `8B.6`. [Bundestag relief-package assessment](https://www.bundestag.de/presse/hib/kurzmeldungen-923970)

- **R062 — 5B/8B:** In July 2022 Scholz initiated a “Concerted Action” involving unions, employers, government, the Bundesbank, and the economic advisory council to address inflation and energy scarcity. He acknowledged that existing relief was insufficient. This is direct evidence of attempted coordination plus an explicit limitation; outcomes remain unresolved. Supports `5B.3`, `5B.6`, `5B.8`, `5B.9`, `8B.1`, `8B.4`, `8B.8`. [Bundestag government questioning](https://www.bundestag.de/dokumente/textarchiv/2022/kw27-de-regierungsbefragung-900498)

- **R063 — 6B:** A 2022 peer-reviewed German study found underuse of mental-health services among asylum-seeking and refugee adolescents relative to reported needs, with language, legal, administrative, and economic barriers. The data were collected in 2019–2020, so this is persistent pre-period service-access context, not a 2022 event. It provides contrary evidence against inferring adequate welfare access from aggregate admissions or funding. Supports `6B.2`, `6B.3`, `6B.6`, `6B.8`. [npj Mental Health Research](https://www.nature.com/articles/s44184-022-00019-2)

- **R064 — 7B:** In August 2022, Cologne prosecutors searched the mailbox of Scholz’s chief-of-staff and identified an email they described as potentially relevant to deletion of calendar and email data. Scholz’s office denied his involvement in the calendar inquiry, and the report stated that evidence of his political influence had not been established. This is documentary scrutiny and contrary evidence, not proof of concealment or obstruction. Supports `7B.3`, `7B.4`, `7B.6`, `7B.7`, `7B.10`. [NDR report](https://www.ndr.de/der_ndr/presse/mitteilungen/Cum-Ex-Affaere-Postfach-von-Scholz-Bueroleiterin-durchsucht%2Cpressemeldungndr23360.html)

- **R065 — 8B/5B:** The Bundestag’s June 2022 budget record documents passage of the federal budget and supplementary budget after a lengthy debate, with 391 votes in favour and 297 against. It establishes formal legislative implementation under coalition and parliamentary constraint, but does not isolate Scholz’s coordination effectiveness. Supports `5B.6`, `8B.2`, `8B.3`, `8B.4`, `8B.8`. [Bundestag budget debate](https://www.bundestag.de/dokumente/textarchiv/2022/kw22-de-generalaussprache-896288)

- **R066 — 8B/5B:** The June 2022 federal cabinet adopted precautionary measures for possible gas shortages, including reserve-power capacity and authority to reduce gas-fired generation. The page returned a rate-limit error after discovery, so this remains **discovery-only** unless independently retrieved with a precise locator. [Federal Ministry search candidate](https://www.bundeswirtschaftsministerium.de/Redaktion/EN/Pressemitteilungen/2022/06/20220608-further-steps-on-the-path-to-creating-independence-from-russian-gas-imports-federal-cabinet-adopts-precautionary-measures-for-the-event-of-an-impending-gas-shortage.html)

### Search and disposition result

- **1B:** Materially improved through target-year nuclear-risk, arms-control, biosecurity, cyber, and autonomous-weapons governance evidence. Nuclear command-and-control and direct Scholz attribution remain unavailable.
- **2B:** Improved through parliamentary delivery chronology, contrary timing criticism, and 2022 export-scale data. Civilian effects, end-use compliance, and negotiation conduct remain unresolved.
- **3B:** Recovered subnational police-complaint findings and contemporaneous journalist-threat records. Federal oversight and Scholz-specific responsibility remain unresolved.
- **4B:** Recovered official disinformation-governance evidence and journalist-safety material. Opposition treatment, appointments, and executive pressure remain unresolved.
- **5B:** Recovered fiscal implementation and coordination evidence. Distributional outcomes and inherited energy responsibility remain incomplete.
- **6B:** Recovered contrary service-access evidence, but its pre-period data require explicit persistence framing. 2022 regional capacity and affordability remain incomplete.
- **7B:** Recovered prosecutor-linked documentary scrutiny and an explicit denial of Scholz involvement. No personal benefit, concealment, obstruction, or final finding is established.
- **8B:** Recovered coalition/parliamentary implementation and crisis-coordination evidence. Cross-portfolio outcomes, adaptation, and personnel management remain thin.
